function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
Below you’ll find quick‑start “cheat sheets” for retrieving **detailed interface data** on three common platforms: | Platform | Typical CLI / Tool | What it shows | |----------|--------------------|---------------| | **Linux/Unix** | `ip link show dev eth0`
`ip addr show dev eth0`
`ethtool eth0` | Interface state, MTU, speed/duplex, driver, MAC, TX/RX counters, errors, flow control | | **macOS** | `networksetup -listallhardwareports`
`ifconfig en0` | Hardware port name, MAC, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, flags (`UP/DOWN`, `RUNNING`) | | **Windows** | `Get-NetIPInterface –InterfaceAlias Ethernet*`
`Get-NetAdapter –Name Ethernet*`
`netsh interface ipv4 show interfaces` | Adapter GUID, MAC, DHCP/VLAN settings, statistics, media type | --- ### 1️⃣ Linux / Unix ```bash # Basic details + MAC & state $ ip link show dev eth0 2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff # Address configuration $ ip addr show dev eth0 2: eth0: <...> inet 192.168.10.5/24 brd 192.168.10.255 scope global dynamic noprefixroute eth0 valid_lft 86399sec preferred_lft 86399sec inet6 fe80::aabb:ccff:fedd:eefc/64 scope link ``` For *driver-level* stats: ```bash $ ethtool -S eth0 # RX/TX packet counts, error rates $ ethtool --show-settings eth0 # Speed, duplex, auto-negotiation ``` If you’re working inside a container or minimal distro without `ethtool`, install it first: ```bash sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install ethtool ``` #### Using SNMP (optional) Many routers/switches expose interface tables via SNMP OIDs such as: - `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8` – ifOperStatus - `.1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16` – ifInOctets Use `snmpwalk -v2c -c public .1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2`. --- ### 2️⃣ macOS ```bash # List all hardware ports and their corresponding BSD names $ networksetup -listallhardwareports Hardware Port: Wi-Fi Device: en0 Ethernet Address: aa-bb-cc-dd-ee-ff # Show full interface config $ ifconfig en0 en0: flags=8863 mtu 1514 options=40000 ether aa:b b:c:d:e:f inet 192.168.1.42 netmask 0xffffff00 broadcast 192.168.1.255 nd6 options=201 media: autoselect status: active ``` To see traffic counters: ```bash $ netstat -i en0 Inter-| Receive Transmit face | bytes packets errs drop fifo frame compressed multicast en0 | 1234567 23456 0 0 0 0 0 0 ``` --- ### 3️⃣ Windows Open **PowerShell** (run as Administrator) and try: ```powershell # Quick overview of adapters PS C:\> Get-NetAdapter | Format-Table Name, Status, MacAddress, LinkSpeed, MediaType # Detailed per-interface properties PS C:\> Get-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias Ethernet* # Statistics (bytes transmitted/received) PS C:\> Get-CimInstance Win32_PerfFormattedData_Tcpip_NetworkAdapterStatistics ` | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq "Ethernet"} ` | Select-Object BytesReceivedPerSec,BytesSentPerSec,PacketsReceivedPerSec,PacketsOutboundErrors ``` Alternatively, use classic CMD utilities: ```cmd C:\> netsh interface ipv4 show interfaces C:\> netsh int tcp show global ``` These will give you metrics such as congestion window size, retransmission count, etc., useful when troubleshooting performance issues. --- ## 📌 Summary Checklist | Step | Action | Command Example | |------|--------|------------------| | 1 | Identify adapter name | `ip link` / `ifconfig` / `Get-NetAdapter` | | 2 | View basic config (MAC/IP/status) | `ip addr` / `ifconfig` / `Get-NetIPAddress` | | 3 | Inspect driver/hardware level | `ethtool` / `sysctl` / `Get-CimInstance` | | 4 | Gather traffic counters | `cat /proc/net/dev` / `netstat` / `Get-NetAdapterStatistics` | | 5 | Check advanced diagnostics | `tcpdump -i eth0` / `wireshark` / `perfmon` | Feel free to let me know what platform you’re targeting or whether you’d like scripts that automate this process!
